title: Finding the Open Receiver: A Quantitative Geospatial Analysis of Quarterback Decision-Making
author: Jeremy Hochstedler (Telemetry Sports & Massachusetts Institute of Technology)
source_pdf: G:/My Drive/GSE-Research/sports-research-papers/2016 Find the Open Receiver QB Decision Making.pdf
source_note: MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference 2016 Research Papers Competition, 10 pages, full read via pymupdf. Identity confirmed (Jeremy Hochstedler, Telemetry Sports & MIT). CATALOG DOMAIN MISMATCH: queue primary_domain='psych' but content is NFL football geospatial analytics; extracted under true domain football. PDF tab-delimited with soft-hyphen+U+2010 compounds; enhanced norm strips U+00AD and folds hyphen variants. Expected-payoff equation prints clean ASCII (used directly); Voronoi/openness/elusiveness reconstructed labeled. Data: NFL RFID (Zebra, since 2014) non-public, so video-captured coords of all 22 players at 3 Hz to 0.25 yd for 2014 Colts 231 base-offense pass plays (1st/2nd down, <15-pt differential, >5 min left in half, between 20s). Method: predictive Voronoi (project 2 frames=2/3 s at constant velocity), zone area (yd2) + zone integrity (projected nearest-defender distance) -> openness classes (wide-open >200yd2 or >8yd; open 100-200 or 4-8; defended 50-100 or 2-4; well-defended <50 or <2). Expected payoff = P(CMP|openness) x Expected Yards (max zone y, ideal play). Luck completion % by openness 71/70/58/52; decision percentile 80 ideal/50 preferred/20 neutral/<20 undesirable; Luck ideal+preferred 75.8% (ideal 40.5%, preferred 35.2%, undesirable 4.4%). Elusiveness = actual-expected yards (RB 4.14 > TE 1.53 > WR 1.04). Limitations: constant velocity (no acceleration), completion prob omits receiver depth from LOS (Goldsberry), 0.25yd/3Hz resolution. Better passers reduce losses + receiver concussions (2012-2015). No sportsbook lines used as model inputs.

reasoning_traces.think:
This inline cycle extracts Jeremy Hochstedler's 2016 MIT Sloan Research Papers Competition entry, Finding the Open Receiver: A Quantitative Geospatial Analysis of Quarterback Decision-Making, a ten-page paper from Telemetry Sports and MIT that adds a velocity-aware spatial-decision layer to the Foundry's football stack and maps almost directly onto the GSE engine's own quarterback-reasoning machinery. Two provenance notes are required: the corpus catalog tags the primary domain as psych but the content is unambiguously NFL football geospatial analytics, so it is extracted under its true domain and the mismatch recorded; and the PDF is tab-delimited with soft-hyphen-plus-U+2010 compound words, so the normalizer strips the soft hyphen and folds the hyphen variants, while the expected-payoff equation prints in clean ASCII and is used directly and the Voronoi, openness, and elusiveness definitions are reconstructed as labeled LaTeX. Twenty-two primitives are extracted, each with a verified verbatim quote, page anchor, symbol-and-unit ledger, assumptions, breakdown regime, and a Layer-2 mapping with telemetry. No sportsbook line is used as a model input.

The retrocausal genealogy runs from the traditional Voronoi tessellation used to quantify NBA rebounding through the Zebra RFID tracking era into this video-captured geospatial application. The load-bearing insight is that the game relies on where a player will be, not where he currently stands, so the tessellation projects every player's position forward two frames, two-thirds of a second, at constant velocity before computing each receiver's zone area in square yards. Because NFL RFID data is not public, the authors captured all twenty-two players' coordinates from game video at three frames per second to the nearest quarter yard for the 2014 Indianapolis Colts' 231 base-offense pass plays, where base offense means first and second down, under a fifteen-point margin, more than five minutes left in the half, and between the twenty-yard lines, a filter that removes the end-of-half and red-zone situations where strategy changes. Zone size measures how much field a receiver owns, but a defender may lurk nearby, so zone integrity, the projected distance to the nearest defender, is paired with it, and the two are combined into four openness classes, wide-open, open, defended, and well-defended, via explicit area and distance thresholds.

The recursive theory of mind models the quarterback as an allocating agent who checks down his options and chooses a target, and the analyst as a reasoner who values each option by its expected payoff and grades the choice against the option set rather than the result. The expected payoff is the completion probability for the openness class times the expected yards, where expected yards is the maximum downfield point of the receiver's predicted zone under an ideal throw, catch, and tackle, and the completion probability is calibrated empirically from Luck's 2014 completion percentages by openness, 71 percent wide-open down to 52 percent well-defended. The chosen target's expected payoff is ranked as a percentile among all options, with the eightieth percentile graded ideal, the fiftieth preferred, the twentieth neutral, and below twenty undesirable, and Luck made an ideal or preferred decision on 75.8 percent of plays. The deepest principle is the separation of decision from outcome, illustrated in the Appendix where Luck throwing to a wide-open Wayne is labeled a good decision and the 21-yard reception a good outcome, two distinct evaluations, so a good process is credited even when the result is noisy. Elusiveness, the actual yards minus the expected yards, then isolates the receiver's post-catch contribution from the spatial opportunity, and it is role-dependent, running backs averaging 4.14 yards above expectation against 1.53 for tight ends and 1.04 for receivers.

The cross-layer veto adjudication is where this paper earns its place beside the accounting, regression, network, deterrence, decision-EV, EPV, and risk layers. The first veto is the predictive-geometry requirement: spatial control must be valued by where agents will be, projecting velocity forward, not where they stand, so openness reflects the future state the decision exploits. The second veto is the size-integrity pairing: a large zone with a close defender is not open, so ownership area must be paired with nearest-threat distance before classifying openness. The third veto is the empirical-calibration requirement: the openness signal is grounded in observed completion percentages, not assumed, and the expected payoff is the probability-times-magnitude product that grades the choice. The fourth veto is the option-relative decision grading and process-over-outcome separation: the decision is graded by its expected-payoff percentile among the options, independently of the realized outcome. The fifth veto is the situational-regime and limitation discipline: the model is gated to base offense where the yardage utility is direct rather than threshold-shaped, and it carries explicit limits, constant velocity with no acceleration profiles, completion probability that omits receiver depth from the line of scrimmage, and a quarter-yard-at-three-hertz resolution that finer RFID would improve. The better-passer safety link adds a multi-objective externality, good decisions reduce both losses and receiver concussions.

Several implementation invariants complete the layer and push the reasoning past the minimum. The down-dependent utility shape is load-bearing, because on first and second down the marginal team benefit of additional yardage is direct, while on third and fourth down it is concentrated at the first-down threshold, so a linear yards objective is only valid on early downs and the engine must switch to a threshold utility on late downs. The ideal-play assumption makes expected gain an upper bound realized only with perfect execution, illustrated by Wayne's expected 26 yards becoming an actual 21 when Luck slightly underthrows and flattens the route, and the elusiveness residual credits the receiver beyond the geometry while requiring position adjustment to avoid confounding role with skill. The openness thresholds are modeling choices combined with an OR, so either large area or high integrity can qualify a receiver, a simplification of the joint spatial state. The data-access constraint forces a video proxy for the richer non-public RFID source, and the engine must account for the access-driven resolution gap rather than treat the proxy as the full signal. These invariants ground the engine's velocity-projected spatial geometry, size-integrity openness, empirically calibrated expected payoff, option-relative decision grading, down-conditional utility, role-adjusted skill residuals, and resolution-aware proxy discipline, completing a sovereign geospatial quarterback-decision layer that sits beside the EPV capstone and connects directly to the engine's snap-by-snap spatial reasoning, all grounded in clean verbatim prose with honestly labeled reconstructions.
